source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
- Provide a unique identifier for the appliance and include the date of the inspection.
- Note down the brand, model, and serial number for identification.
- Clearly describe the type of appliance (e.g., microwave, kettle, toaster, refrigerator).
3. Document the visual inspection findings.
- Record visible signs of wear, damage, or misuse (e.g., frayed cords, cracked housing, burnt switches).
- Indicate whether all safety labels and user instructions are present and legible.
- Note any unusual odors or excessive heat on the appliance surface.
4. Record findings from formal test procedures.
- Use a recognised PAT (Portable Appliance Testing) procedure and record all test results.
- Document any anomalies discovered during the earth continuity, insulation resistance, insulation leakage, and earch leakage tests.
- Record details of any warning or error messages displayed during the checks.
5. Identify the failure(s) and safety issues related to failed tests.
- Specify
